title.narrative: Activity under preparation Climate change adaptation through watershed, forest and disaster risk management and governance TOP UP SIDA

description.narrative: On May 31, 2023, the EU and Sweden signed a ¿20 million contribution agreement to support Bolivia in adapting to climate change through watershed, forest, and disaster risk management. Running from June 2023 to May 2027, the program aims to protect the environment and promote sustainable development.This initiative is unique as it involves civil society organizations rather than specific projects, fostering collaboration at multiple levels. This approach has improved interactions between civil society and government, influencing public policy and promoting sustainable practices. Key achievements include better forest fire management, a shift in Bolivia's climate change policy, and the development of sustainable productive models. The program has also highlighted the importance of building trust among partners and the need for stronger environmental governance.Over the past seven decades, Bolivia has lost 13% of its original forest cover, with deforestation rates among the highest globally. This has led to significant CO2 emissions, biodiversity loss, and increased vulnerability to natural disasters. In 2024, Bolivia faced a major environmental disaster with 12.6 million hectares burned due to wildfires. Deforestation is driven by land conversion for agriculture and cattle ranching, exacerbated by weak governmental responses and poor coordination. The Amazon rainforest, crucial for global climate stability, is nearing a tipping point due to deforestation, combined with the negative effects of climate change. Bolivia is among the ten countries most affected worldwide. Indigenous territories play a key role in protecting forests, but environmental and territorial rights issues persist. The recent opening of Bolivia to carbon markets offers a chance for better environmental management.Although the current contribution has achieved great success in the areas of intervention, a deeper, more comprehensive approach is needed to address these issues especially considering new objectives of the MIP¿s Priority Area 1 ¿Environment, Climate Change and Inclusive Economic Development.The alignment between the EU¿s and Sweden¿s objectives has shown that important synergies can be created by working more closely together. This complementarity provides a basis for effectively addressing some of the environmental challenges that Bolivia faces and for creating governance spaces in the area. This is acutely needed considering the challenges that Bolivia is currently experiencing and the variety of opinions and positions on the subject.The current action document proposes an extension of activities for each component with an additional ¿4 million, extending the timeframe until December 2027. The interventions will focus on four key components i) Conservation and Preservation of Ecosystems, ii) Promotion of Sustainable Production Models, iii) Strengthening of Environmental Governance and iv) Economic Empowerment of Women.It will be based on a landscape approach, aiming to integrate forest protection with sustainable production and the restoration of degraded areas. Although each component will include a variety of projects implemented by different organizations, many of these projects will work synergistically across components. Additionally, the component related to the economic empowerment of women and gender equity will be addressed transversally across the other three components.The different projects within the intervention will focus on:¿Ecosystem Protection: Supporting national and subnational governments in establishing new conservation areas, strengthening protected areas, comprehensive fire management, and integrated forest management.¿Promotion of Sustainable Production Models:
